children: Elon Musk unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 with a stainless-steel, angular design that looked unlike any pickup on the road. The event at Tesla's
design studio in Hawthorne, California invoked a

promised a starting price under $40K, a 500-mile top range, and production by 2021. Delays, redesigns, and manufacturing problems pushed deliveries back until late November 2023, and prices came in far higher than promised. Reddit
co-founder Alexis Ohanian was among the first owners.
An early public demo of the Cybertruck is remembered for the “armor glass” windows that shattered when a steel ball was thrown at them. The early Foundation Series cost around $100K, and Tesla
later added a cheaper all-wheel-drive trim and a rear-wheel-drive version in 2025.
In reality, demand never matched the hype. While Tesla
claimed more than a million reservations, those were refundable deposits, and actual sales were only a fraction of that ambitious tally. During an earnings conference call, Musk once stated Tesla

could build 250K trucks a year, yet annual sales reportedly stayed far below that. Kelley Blue Book estimated Cybertruck sales of 39K in 2024 and just over 20K in 2025. The electric truck's reputation was also dented by repeated recalls, including problems with the accelerator pedal and body panels. Finally, analysts noted Elon Musk's high-profile political activity may have curbed some demand.
The Cybertruck entered a field of electric and conventional pickups. Its closest rivals were the Rivian

Silverado EV and GMC's Hummer EV competed on range and luxury, and the Ram 1500 REV was another planned electric entrant. Of course, the Cybertruck also had to contend with the gas-powered F-150, Silverado, and Ram 1500, which have long dominated the truck market and offer more traditional towing and work capability.

Earlier in the week, Elon Musk said Tesla (TSLAA) will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production, which is Tesla's

disruptive robotaxi. The future of the Cybertruck plans remains unclear, although Elon Musk confirmed it was the end of an era in a X reply. If the timeline holds, production would end roughly three and a half years after the first customer deliveries.
